verdict: finalist (conditional) - vertical = small/mid CPA firms: 1,062 active IL CPA firm licences (680 Chicago-area) [A]; CPA-specific PH seats list $1,400-2,400+ plus management fee [B]; IRC 7216 consent/SSN-safeguard and FTC Safeguards vendor-oversight rules favour a compliant specialist [A]; decisive: EOR at $599-699/worker-month cuts seat contribution from ~38% to ~9%, so contractor/PH-entity structure decides viability; gates: supply test <=$1,200/mo salary asks, 2 prepaid pilot seats, >=50% renew past 30 April
note: Driver model (customer = firm account, 1.4 seats x $2,400, 38% GM, 2.5%/mo churn, 1.2 founder wins/mo): base yr-3 op $231k on $1.33M revenue (~36 accounts/~59 seats), peak funding $13k, breakeven m8; conservative yr-3 -$4k; optimistic model $2.0M treated as a ceiling (high = judgment). Stresses: win -40% -> $151k; GM -10pts -> $99k; competitor response -> $115k. Churn data MISSING; IL new-CPA issuance down ~25% from 2016-19 levels [A]; PE roll-up (ORBA->Citrin Cooperman) [D].

verdict: drop - the done-for-you service is free or bundled in exactly this segment: Clairelist offers UNFI deduction recovery to small food brands at $0 (68% disputes won), SPS leads with free audits and flat-fee/take-rate pricing, Glimpse offers 3-months-free to $1-30M brands; no contingency % is published anywhere (only adjacent FBA 'from 20%'); a $3M UNFI brand yields ~$115/mo contribution; revisit only as an add-on to a broader CPG back-office service
note: Driver model (ARPC $840 = $8M x 3% x 35% invalid x 60% recovered x 20% fee; $5k backlog fee; 0.84 wins/mo; 3%/mo churn; analyst per 15 brands): base yr-3 op $149k on 21 brands rests on E-level fee and win rate; conservative $4k; optimistic model $1.1M not credible. Deductions 1-5% (SPS) to 3-8% of sales and 65-80% invalid shortage claims (RVCF via UCS) [D]. UNFI window conflict: 12 months vs 30-60 days. Distributor relationships of all 25 named Midwest brands MISSING.
